newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Bomb rocks regional parliament in Russian Caucasus.
newsitem.headline: Bomb rocks regional parliament in Russian Caucasus.

text.p: A bomb explosion rocked the local parliament building in the southern Russian region of Kabardino-Balkaria in the early hours of Wednesday, Itar-Tass news agency quoted a parliamentary spokesman as saying.

No one was hurt when the device went off in a cellar, breaking the windows of the building in the regional capital Nalchik, about 100 km from the border with Chechnya, where Moslem separatists have wrested control from the Russia army.
There was no claim of responsibility. Kabardino-Balkaria is due to hold a presidential election on January 12 in which President Valery Kokov is the only candidate.
But Interfax news agency quoted a regional security official saying there was no evidence the blast was politically motivated and that it could have been "simple hooliganism."
While Chechnya has seen by far the greatest violence, ethnic tensions and separatist tendencies are endemic throughout the turbulent North Caucasus.
In November a group of local politicians urged the Balkar people, about a tenth of the region's 650,000 population, to break away and form their own republic.
Kokov condemned the move and the parliament promptly banned the group, whose demands reopened old inter-ethnic scars.

In 1944, Soviet dictator Josef Stalin deported the entire mountain nation of the Balkars, along with the Chechens and several other small North Caucasus tribes, to the steppes of Kazakhstan, accusing them of helping the German invaders.

After Stalin's death in 1953, the Balkars were allowed to return, only to find their Kabardin neighbours, who had lived on the plains, installed in their mountain lands. The two nations were united into a single semi-autonomous republic by Moscow.
In June last year a bomb blast ripped through a passenger bus in Nalchik, killing four people and injuring 24. Nobody claimed responsibility.
